name: aged-lock-packs-collected
note: Second campaign of phase F part 2 (random-1867481925586694457): a time jump past the 6 h lock staleness, compact reaps the backup's lock and its stale session marker and deletes its packs as orphans (and its segment), the backup's head then publishes entries naming them and its next backup's fold carries them on: the index names absent packs. Fixed by 04 steps 5 and 8. Since 04 step 5 (phase F part 7) young orphans are kept: the backup's packs are about 6 h old on the store's clock at the compact, younger than T_pack, so compact keeps them and only AgedLockReaped is left (the head PUT outside the lock). aged-lock-packs-collected-old-packs shows it with packs older than T_pack. Young orphans kept since 04 step 5 (phase F part 7): this schedule must stay as expected. Since phase F part 8c (04 step 7, young segments) the backup's later fold no longer writes its first segment's entries into a base: that segment, which compact's index GC collected (it was older than T_idx and no head named it yet), is about 6 h old at the fold, younger than T_pack, so the fold keeps it named after the new base, and the head names an absent segment: AgedLockSegmentCollected (the same aged reap and late head; before 8c the fold carried the entries from the backup's local cache into a base and hid the loss; a segment missing from the fold's listing reads young, so no later jump changes this). Fixed by 04 step 8. Since 04 step 8 (phase F part 9) this runs on the fallback store, which keeps the hazard; aged-lock-packs-collected-conditional is the same case on a conditional store. Since phase F part 10b2 the segment (about 6 h old at the compact) is younger than INDEX_OBJECT_GRACE (12 h, T_pack) and compact keeps it: AgedLockReaped only, as between 04 step 5 and 8c (unchanged schedule; aged-lock-packs-collected-old-packs shows the packs collected).
